## Design note

The battering ram with a badge. Nearly seven tonnes of armour on a 4x4 truck frame: glacial off the line, done at 140 km/h, stops like a lorry and leans like one — but whatever it hits moves, and whatever hits it stops. Captains roll it into roadblocks and use it to end pursuits by pushing the target off the road.

## How this car breaks

Armoured box on a full-length ladder frame with a heavy push bar and doubled bumper beam: almost nothing a car can do reaches the structure, and the battering-ram bar soaks the first hits. What does break is outside the armour — wheels, steering and suspension at the corners, and the tires (it is heavy enough to tear its own hubs on a kerb strike). The high CG means a hard side hit at the wheels can trip it.

## Inertia

Box approximation about the CG, scaled for mass concentration (`k < 1`: mass near the centre, e.g. mid-engine; `k → 1`: mass at the ends):

```
I_roll  = k_r · m·(W² + H²)/12
I_pitch = k_p · m·(L² + H²)/12
I_yaw   = k_y · m·(W² + L²)/12
```

| roll | 8169 | 0.90 | 7350 |
| pitch | 26556 | 0.95 | 25230 |

## Drivetrain

6-speed automatic with torque converter, part-time 4WD driven locked (fixed 45/55 split), clutch-type rear LSD; top speed set by the limiter in 6th (fleet governor). Layout **AWD, 45 % front**; front diff: open; rear diff: clutch LSD, preload 150 N·m, power ramp 0.60, coast ramp 0.20. Torque converter: stall 1900 rpm, 2.0× at stall, couples 1:1 from 2300 rpm (class-typical for the gearbox). Clutch capacity 1.60 × peak torque = 1620 N·m. Shift time 0.40 s.

## Suspension

Springs from ride frequency, `k = m_s·(2πf)²` with sprung corner mass `m_s = axle load/2 − unsprung`; dampers `c = 2ζ·√(k·m_s)`, ζ = 0.30 bump, rebound = 1.5 × bump.

| Axle | m_s | f | Wheel rate k | Bump c | Rebound c | Travel |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Front | 1512 kg | 1.55 Hz | 143500 N/m | 8840 N·s/m | 13260 N·s/m | 0.20 m |
| Rear | 1509 kg | 1.75 Hz | 182400 N/m | 9950 N·s/m | 14920 N·s/m | 0.20 m |

Anti-roll bars from a roll-gradient target of 4.0°/g with 60% of roll stiffness at the front. Roll arm h − h_rc = 0.999 m (roll centres 0.08 m F / 0.12 m R). Required total K_φ = m·g·arm/φ = 955032 N·m/rad; springs give k·t²/2 = 258933 F / 312102 R N·m/rad; bars supply the rest as `arb_n_per_m = K_bar/t²` = **87000 F / 20400 R N/m** (clamped at ≥ 0). Resulting gradient 4.0°/g, front share 60%. Bump stops 1200000 N/m.

Alignment: camber +0.0° F / +0.0° R, toe +0.10° F / +0.00° R (+ = in), caster 4.0°.

## Brakes

Full-pedal line pressure 100 bar.

- Front: 410 mm disc, pistons per side 66 mm + 66 mm → A = 68.4 cm², r_eff = D/2 − 25 mm = 180 mm, pad μ = 0.42: T = 2·μ·p·A·r_eff = 2·0.42·100 bar·68.4 cm²·0.180 m = **10346 N·m**
- Rear: 410 mm disc, pistons per side 66 mm + 66 mm → A = 68.4 cm², r_eff = D/2 − 25 mm = 180 mm, pad μ = 0.42: T = 2·μ·p·A·r_eff = 2·0.42·100 bar·68.4 cm²·0.180 m = **10346 N·m**

Lock check at 1 g on μ = 1 (load transfer m·a·h/L): front needs 9936 N·m/wheel (capacity 1.04×), rear needs 3040 N·m/wheel (capacity 3.40×).

`wp_vehicle` gives the axle `bias_front` favours its full `max_torque_*` and scales the other by (1 − b)/b, so `max_torque_*` holds the caliper capacity per wheel and `bias_front` acts as the proportioning valve: the rear is trimmed to the same lock margin as the front (ideal rear = T_f · lock_r/lock_f = 3167 N·m), never boosted above its caliper capacity. Rear capacity exceeds that, so `bias_front` = T_r/(T_r + ideal) = **0.766** → delivered 10350 N·m front / 3162 N·m rear per wheel at full pedal. Handbrake 4140 N·m per rear wheel.

## Steering

Ratio 20.0:1. Kerb-to-kerb turning circle 16.0 m → outer-front path radius 7.89 m, rear-axle-centre radius 5.93 m → mean road-wheel lock δ = atan(L/R) = **0.576 rad (33.0°)** (outer 29.2°, inner 37.7° at full Ackermann; `ackermann_frac` 0.80). Rack speed 1.0 rad/s.

## Damage lattice (`data/lattices/sentinel_breacher.json`)

344 nodes, 2243 beams, 9 detachables, 21 component mounts.

- Generated with `gen-lattice --id sentinel_breacher --profile suv --width 2.45 --length 6.2 --height 2.9 --wheelbase 3.85 --mass 1496.4 --car-mass 6802.0 --clearance 0.35 --front-overhang 1.0 --strength 1.3` (22% of vehicle mass in the lattice; strength from durability class 5).
- Era `2010s`: gen-lattice's default HSS passenger cell kept as is.
- Steel hood: 159 hood beams aluminum → mild_steel.
- Chrome steel bumpers: 180 bumper beams pp_bumper → mild_steel.
- Detachables: steel bumpers ×2.3 break impulse / ×4 mass; steel hood ×1.4 / ×1.6.
- Body-on-frame: 20 cab-floor rail nodes relabelled FrameLeft/FrameRight; 18 under-cab rail beams → hss 9.55e-04 m² so the ladder frame runs bumper to bumper.
- Cargo box: 40 Cabin nodes behind the seat partition (y < -0.09 m, just behind the front doors) relabelled FrameRear — the passenger cell is the cab only, so cargo-box hits are body damage, not cabin intrusion.
- Push bar: 4 extra Accessory-region nodes 0.10 m ahead of the bumper (z 0.45/0.95 m), hss 2.4e-03 m² tubes bolted to the bumper-beam rail nodes with 1.8e-03 m² mounts; detachable group 8, 150000 N·s, 120 kg. Front bumper beam ×2 (2 beams), as gen-lattice's cruiser profile does.
- Police package: heavy-duty components fail at × the stock intrusion (Battery ×2.0, Engine ×1.5, FuelTank ×2.0, Radiator ×2.0, SteeringRack ×1.5, SuspensionFL ×1.5, SuspensionFR ×1.5); front bumper fixings ×3.0 detach impulse.
